title: Finite-family Fourier estimate from a target
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ to the signs, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $m$ be a natural number. Given $m$ cube inputs for each $S\in\mathcal F$, form labeled samples by evaluating $f$ at those inputs, then use the labeled finite-family Fourier estimator to produce the sparse Fourier hypothesis.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the dimension-$n$ Boolean cube to the signs
$\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
For each $S\in\mathcal F$, $m$ cube inputs are supplied
